findings.problem: The focused Electron runtime test is not included in the default npm test command; npm test only runs the ERD tool tests, so the SS-002 startup repair can regress while the default test entrypoint remains green.
findings.proposed_fix: Include tests/electron-runtime.test.mjs in the default test script, or make npm test delegate to both the existing ERD tool tests and npm run test:electron.

findings.problem: The BrowserWindow uses good isolation defaults but does not install explicit navigation or new-window policies, so renderer links or unexpected navigations are not constrained to the app-owned drawdb:// surface.
findings.proposed_fix: Add will-navigate and setWindowOpenHandler controls that keep app-owned drawdb:// navigation internal, deny unexpected windows by default, and open explicitly allowlisted external URLs through the OS browser.

findings.problem: The supplied user-smoke result reports startup and core-flow success, but the accompanying manifest and logs show a web-baseline Vite smoke, not an Electron launch of the built desktop runtime.
findings.proposed_fix: Add Electron-specific smoke evidence that launches the built desktop runtime without Vite, verifies the drawdb://desktop/editor route or visible editor, and stores a screenshot or comparable runtime diagnostic.

checks_run.summary: Exited 0 after listing the src and tests directory trees, including src/electron and tests; no Python compile errors were emitted.

electron_startup_correctness.justification: The repaired main process registers a privileged drawdb scheme, serves files from the desktop renderer build through protocol.handle, and loads drawdb://desktop/editor, which matches the BrowserRouter /editor route. No High or Critical startup blocker was found.

focused_runtime_test.justification: tests/electron-runtime.test.mjs covers the intended scaffold and protocol shape, but the default npm test entrypoint does not execute it.

npm_test_and_build_behavior.justification: package.json keeps npm run build as the web build and adds separate desktop build scripts. The default npm test script remains limited to ERD tool tests while test:electron is separate.

electron_security.justification: contextIsolation, nodeIntegration false, sandbox true, and a narrow frozen preload are positive defaults; explicit navigation and new-window controls are still missing.

production_asset_loading.justification: dist-desktop/index.html uses relative built assets, dist-electron contains main.cjs and preload.cjs, and the source protocol handler falls back to index.html for app routes while blocking paths outside the renderer directory.
